title: Copies of K₄,₄ in K₃,₅-free graphs

comparators.scope: Fourteen explicit fixed targets covering all ten numbered results, preliminary alteration and distinct-copy injection.
Main graph-existence theorem with an added hypothesis. Rejection detail: added premise on Verification.theorem_1.
Main graph-existence statement with an intentionally illegal proof dependency. Rejection detail: unauthorized axiom in Verification.theorem_1.

main_results.scope: For every sufficiently large n, a bipartite K₃,₅-free graph on n vertices has at least c*n³ unoriented K₄,₄ copies; theorem_1_theta gives the two-sided extremal bound.
Any three distinct cap points have linearly independent homogeneous vectors over a field with the stated nonsquare parameter.
Rank-three plane sections, exact exceptional-family counts and incidences, and the identity-family point-deletion bound.
Monic quartic witnesses yield many nonexceptional four-point planes with an explicit positive constant and field-size threshold.
Designated copies through an edge inject into a Grassmannian, giving the 6*q⁴ bound; both controlled-plane intersections have size at most two.
Every valid simultaneous pruning outcome is K₃,₅-free; independent finite choices yield the stated designated-copy survival bound.
Joint pairing selection, preliminary survival, and an injection from distinct surviving designated pairs to graph copies.
